note: Written by hand from the reading and the tests named; held by tools/asvs_checklist.py --check. basis: shown (a test named in 'test' shows it), hypothesis (read from code), not_run.

findings.claim: Behind Caddy every browser shares one address, so five wrong guesses lock a named person out on every PC.
findings.expected: ASVS 2.2.1: anti-automation must not allow a lock-out attack; D-279 counts failures per account and address.
findings.happened: Neither the identity overlay nor deploy/install.sh sets TB_CONSOLE_FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS; uvicorn keeps its default 127.0.0.1 (deploy/docker-compose.yml:366), so the console sees Caddy's address for everyone.

findings.claim: The session cookie has no __Host- prefix.
findings.expected: ASVS 3.4.4: a session cookie named __Host-..., Secure, Path=/, no Domain.
findings.happened: The cookie is named tb_console; a sibling host name (Authelia's is a sub-name in the example) could set one.

findings.claim: A person cannot see or end their other sessions, and a new sign-in leaves older ones alive.
findings.expected: ASVS 3.3.4: a person can list active sessions and end any or all.
findings.happened: No page lists sessions; UserStore.end_sessions is called by no page; new_session (auth.py:757) ends nothing.
findings.full_review: J V3 'an older session survives a new sign-in' (confirmed by reading)

findings.claim: A break-glass grant opens on the session alone, with no fresh password or code.
findings.expected: ASVS 3.7.1: a sensitive action asks for a fresh sign-in or second check, as signing does (identity.py:307).
findings.happened: POST /breakglass needs only the CSRF token, a reason and a note.

findings.claim: A password longer than 256 characters is accepted when chosen and never signs in.
findings.expected: ASVS 2.1.2 and 2.1.3: long passwords allowed, more than 128 may be refused, none cut short.
findings.happened: check_password_policy has no maximum; the sign-in passes password[:256], which never matches the hash of the whole password, so the owner is locked out of their own account.

findings.claim: A password history of five is enforced, which ASVS 2.1.10 says not to do.
findings.expected: ASVS 2.1.10: no history rule. D-447 chose a history of five after the MHLW guideline v7.0: a recorded ruling.
findings.happened: The owner's own change refuses the last five passwords. Plan 8's exit for V9 asks for no 'does not meet' in V2, so the ruling and the plan disagree: the owner rules which holds.

findings.claim: In PRODUCTION no breached-password check runs unless the operator supplies the list; nothing warns.
findings.expected: ASVS 2.1.7: every new password is checked against a breached list.
findings.happened: Unset TB_CONSOLE_BREACHED_PASSWORDS_FILE means no check; no list ships; no doctor or installer check names it (grep of tools/ and deploy/ found no 'breached').

findings.claim: The password fields have no strength meter and no show-password control, and refuse spaces at the ends.
findings.happened: None of the three in login, account, first sign-in or first-run pages; check_password_policy refuses white space at either end (auth.py:254).

findings.claim: Password hashes have no secret pepper.
findings.expected: ASVS 2.4.5: a second derivation with a secret kept apart from the hashes.
findings.happened: scrypt over the password and its stored salt only; a copy of the auth schema is enough for offline guessing.

findings.claim: Local accounts cannot use a security key; only directory accounts can (through Authelia).
findings.expected: ASVS 2.3.2: security keys can be enrolled and used.
findings.happened: TOTP only for local accounts (D-447 'Open'); the administrator's own account is local.

findings.claim: The holder is not told of a replayed code, of their own password change or of a new sign-in.
findings.expected: ASVS 2.2.3, 2.5.5, 2.8.5: the holder is told after a change of a factor and of a replayed code.
findings.happened: Notices exist only when someone else resets or opens the account (D-719); a replayed code is audited only (identity.py:503).

findings.claim: Sign-out removes the session cookie without the flags it was set with.
findings.expected: The removal carries Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict like the cookie (firstrun.py:243 does).
findings.happened: Set-Cookie: tb_console=""; Max-Age=0; Path=/; SameSite=lax. The session row is deleted on the server first, so no session survives; Low because nothing is exposed.

findings.claim: Database, mail and KEK passwords are environment variables; the TOTP key is a plain file in the console volume.
findings.expected: ASVS 6.4.1: a secrets-management solution; 2.10.3: service passwords resist offline recovery.
findings.happened: deploy/.env reaches every container (env_file, docker-compose.yml:31); each service's database password is in its TB_DB_URL. Tokens and the model key are files (docker-compose.secrets.yml), the rest is not.

findings.claim: A chart number typed in free text (a break-glass note, a reason) stays in the audit, which is never erased.
findings.expected: ASVS 7.1.2: no identifying data in logs; plan 8 criterion 8: nothing of a person stays after erasure.
findings.happened: mask_detail masks by key name and 'key=value' only; breakglass.py:211 writes the typed note into the audit detail (path read from code; the mask shown by the test).

findings.claim: A service not listed in CALLERS accepts any service's token.
findings.expected: The module's own docstring (line 11): a callee 'accepts only the callers of CALLERS (403 otherwise)'.
findings.happened: allowed() returns True for an unlisted callee. Every deployed service is listed today, so the gap is latent; the trace store's HTTP app (unsigned role headers) is started by no compose file.

findings.claim: No threat model is on file.
findings.expected: ASVS 1.1.2: a threat model for the design and each change.
findings.happened: docs/security/ has ten files and none is a threat model; none in docs/validation/.

findings.claim: A password an administrator resets never expires until it is used.
findings.expected: ASVS 2.3.1: a system-made first or reset secret expires after a short time.
findings.happened: random_password() with must_change, but no expiry; a new account's code expires in 24 hours.

findings.claim: A break-glass grant is stored before its audit event is written, so a failed write leaves an open grant the audit trail does not show.
findings.expected: The 13:30 severity rule: an audit trail that can be wrong is High; ASVS 7.1.3 security events are logged.
findings.happened: bg.open commits at line 205; au.append('console.breakglass_open') follows at line 211. The steward's review list reads the grant store, so the grant is still seen there.

findings.claim: A typed mark note stays in the tab's session storage after sign-out and is put back for the next person who opens that patient in that tab.
findings.expected: ASVS 8.2.2: data in browser storage is cleared when the session ends. D-777 keeps the note on purpose.
findings.happened: Nothing clears tb-note:* at sign-out; on a shared clinic PC the next account sees the earlier person's note.
